answer.evidence: The main body is a tall vertical sheet of ice, rows 1-80, made of vertical streaks. Its upper end (rows 1-5, width 25-31) is a flat light band with no front-edge line and no eave shadow. It reads as a rim or rounded end, not a top surface. The only real top-down surface is the elliptical pool at the base: widths go 30, 29, 30, then 32 at rows 85-90, then narrow to 22 and 16 at rows 94-95, so it spans about rows 81-95. That pool is a separate base part. The ice column above it is drawn purely as a front elevation.

Texture is vertical highlight streaks, banded shadows and a rim-lit pool. It has no large flat areas, with near-flat coverage at 1%. answer.evidence: The tall ice wall (rows 6-80) is a vertical front face of about 75 rows. Its top rows 1-5 form a light, wide band (width 25-31) that is weak evidence of a top, with a white highlight line at row 6. The base is a clear ellipse (rows 81-95): width goes 29-30, then 32 at rows 85-90, then narrows 30, 28, 26, 22, 16, and it has shaded ice or water contents with a dark rim. That is a horizontal surface seen from above, so the object has a top surface and a front face. The top cap is weak, so this reading rests mostly on the base ellipse.

styleAnswer.evidence: The icefall is a smooth tapered column with a pool at its base. Its blue-tinted dark edges are material-toned, not black (0% neutral dark edge pixels). It has about 5 ice steps from white highlight through pale blue to mid blue and a deep blue shadow. Vertical streak highlights and a shaded pool rim add some structure. Measured density is 9 visible tones per tile, with 1% near-flat coverage. That is above tree-1a786c (7) but far below tree-d43edd (29), the richer reference. By eye, the body is mostly one pale-blue ramp with regular vertical streaks. It has no per-clump or per-chunk shading, no irregular ice facets or icicle detail, and little grain, so it reads cleaner and flatter than the Beodeul references. It also lacks their layered clusters, and it looks closer to a gradient-filled sticker than to hand-shaded texture. This is borderline, and with that doubt I fail it.
